open_points.subject: context
open_points.question: Does `verification:transport_guard_client_portal` denote the accepted Factory check, whose transport guard reads `time.monotonic()` directly, or a coordinator-updated check that requires `transport_guard` to obtain the elapsed reading from `system_clock`?
options: The witness is the accepted Factory check and therefore cannot assert CLK-002 as now defined.
The witness was updated after the coordinator introduced `system_clock` and asserts indirect monotonic-clock access.
The witness checks only rate-limit behavior and does not establish the clock-source part of CLK-002.
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a coordinator-updated verification check and bind the witness to the revision that injects or substitutes `system_clock`.

witness.initial: The accepted Factory spec and its transport guard read `time.monotonic()` directly; the coordinator later introduces `system_clock` as the only host-clock reader.
events: The coordinator changes A28 so `transport_guard` must request one elapsed reading from `system_clock` per viewer-entry request.
State 3 adds `verification:transport_guard_client_portal` as a witness for CLK-002 without identifying a changed verification revision.
A careful implementer reuses the accepted Factory check; another updates the check to fail on direct `time.monotonic()` access.
outcomes: The named check passes a transport guard that reads the host monotonic clock directly, so it does not prove CLK-002.
The named check passes only when the transport guard obtains its reading through `system_clock`, so it proves CLK-002.
witness.observer: The State 3 reviewer or verification runner relying on the witness to establish the new clock-source boundary.
